content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text resolves a link against the challenger's Isaiah 7:14 rows by treating the sign's sense as open rather than weighing chain against chain by footing.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"The phrase 'leaving the sign's sense open' — reading 1: the verse's open sense alone decides, which K-C retires; reading 2: the whole chain by footing leaves the sign's sense open.","why":"Because K-C requires chain-against-chain weighing by footing and retires the open-sense/stating-verse test, the judge's reliance on the sign's sense being open rather than on footing breaches the rule."}
